title: The Real Tower of Babel?
author: QUILL
notes: Etemenanki link framed as a hypothesis. Herodotus cited as description, not proof. Not-proven line in beat 11.

beats.text: Was the Tower of Babel a real building?
Genesis 11 says they used brick for stone and bitumen for mortar.
beats.display: Brick for stone, bitumen for mortar

beats.text: Babel is Hebrew for Babylon, in what is now Iraq.
Babylon's great ziggurat was Etemenanki: 'house of the foundation of heaven and earth.'
beats.say: Babylon's great ziggurat was EH-teh-MEN-an-kee: house of the foundation of heaven and earth.
beats.label: ETEMENANKI

beats.text: Herodotus described a stepped tower of eight tiers there.
beats.say: Her-ODD-oh-tus described a stepped tower of eight tiers there.

beats.text: Today only its foundation survives, near the modern city of Hillah.
beats.say: Today only its foundation survives, near the modern city of HIL-lah.

beats.text: Another candidate: the ziggurat at Borsippa, now called Birs Nimrud.
beats.say: Another candidate: the ziggurat at bor-SIP-ah, now called BEERS nim-ROOD.

beats.text: King Nebuchadnezzar II says in inscriptions that he rebuilt it.
beats.say: King NEB-uh-kud-NEZ-er the Second says in inscriptions that he rebuilt it.
beats.label: NEBUCHADNEZZAR II REBUILDS

beats.text: Genesis puns on the name: Babel sounds like the Hebrew for 'confuse.'
Many scholars link the story to Etemenanki, but Borsippa still has its fans.
beats.say: Many scholars link the story to EH-teh-MEN-an-kee, but bor-SIP-ah still has its fans.

beats.text: Plainly: the link is a hypothesis, and no tower is proven to be Babel's.
Babylon's tower fell to dust, but its story did not.
Real ziggurat or pure legend? What do you think?

youtube.description:
Babylon had a giant ziggurat called Etemenanki, and Herodotus described a stepped tower there.
Linking it to Genesis 11 is a hypothesis, not a proven fact.
